{"id": "40:28/q18", "question": "What are the clear proofs?", "turns_on": "Whether the proofs are Moses' miracles, arguments, or rulings.", "positions": [{"id": "40:28/q18/p1", "position": "Clear signs establishing Moses' truth", "reasons": "JISHUMI, d. 494: Since God is not a body, bodily organs such as hand and face cannot be affirmed of Him. TABRISI, d. 548: The clear proofs of Moses' truth include the staff, the hand, and other miracles. IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597: The clear proofs are signs demonstrating Moses' truthfulness. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671: The clear signs that came with Moses are the nine signs. BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685: The numerous proofs are miracles and demonstrations that establish Moses' truthfulness. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393: After a tactful opening, the believer advances to explicit endorsement of Moses: clear proofs establish his truth, and the God he names is their Lord too. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393: Al-bayyināt means clear proofs of Moses’s truth. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393: The threatened portion may befall them in this life or the next; the signs themselves could bring disasters such as the flood, locusts, and the remaining signs. TABATABAI, d. 1402: The question condemns their plan to kill Moses; the signs establish that God is their Lord too, so Moses brought them truth from their Lord. ISLAHI-TADABBUR: Moses’ clear signs prove he is God-sent; only the blind can refuse to recognize his mission. MUQATIL: hand and staff; liar harmed by own lie; truthful warning harms opponents TAB-FULL: kill Moses for saying Lord God; signs show truth; أن accusative TAB-FULL: signs staff and hand prove Moses TAB-FULL: Ibn Ishaq staff and hand ZAJJAJ: signs prophethood proving truth MAWARDI-FULL: Yahya proofs staff hand flood 7:130"}, {"id": "40:28/q18/p2", "position": "Arguments proving monotheism", "reasons": "RAZI-FULL, d. 606: The believer's phrase “my Lord is God” points to monotheism, while “clear proofs” refers to evidence for it, including Moses' statements in 20:50 and 26:24. | mentions 20:50, 26:24 ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745: The proofs are evidence for monotheism, as in the debates with Pharaoh recorded in Ta Ha and al-Shu'ara'. | mentions 20:49, 26:23"}, {"id": "40:28/q18/p3", "position": "Moses' lawful and unlawful rulings", "reasons": "MAWARDI-FULL: Suddi proofs lawful unlawful"}]}

{"id": "40:28/q20", "question": "Why say 'from your Lord'?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "40:28/q20/p1", "position": "It reminds the audience that Moses' Lord is theirs", "reasons": "KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538: The question forcefully condemns the atrocious killing of an inviolate person for no reason but his truthful confession; the believer also reminds them that the God he names is their Lord too, softening their fury. KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538: Moses had brought multiple mighty signs from the one he calls Lord, who is not only his Lord but theirs; the reminder draws them toward acknowledging Him. BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685: Calling the signs from your Lord presses them to acknowledge the point and gently leads them toward admitting it. NASAFI-FULL, d. 710: The phrase means “because he says”; the believer condemns killing a protected person when the only alleged offense is speaking the truth that Allah is his Lord—and theirs too. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745: Asking whether they will kill a man merely for saying his Lord is God is a forceful rebuke: their only basis for killing him is his truthful statement, despite proofs from their own Lord. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745: Saying the proofs came from your Lord, rather than only his Lord, subtly invites Pharaoh's people to acknowledge that Moses' God is theirs too. BIQAI-FULL, d. 885: Since God is Moses' Lord and benefactor, Moses should acknowledge Him; the audience's own dependence on the same Lord should likewise lead them to acknowledge Him. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270: Calling God the Lord of all of them gently draws them toward admitting that Moses’ Lord is their Lord too. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393: After a tactful opening, the believer advances to explicit endorsement of Moses: clear proofs establish his truth, and the God he names is their Lord too. TABATABAI, d. 1402: The question condemns their plan to kill Moses; the signs establish that God is their Lord too, so Moses brought them truth from their Lord. ISLAHI-TADABBUR: The believer reminds Pharaoh’s court that the Lord Moses represents is also their Lord; their error is treating others as lords beside Him."}]}
